text:
LIVE ON WOG, measured by m1: 46 cells, three present-term sets -- 20 with no terms (external, never blended), 13 with 5 terms (present-weight 3.200), 13 with 6 (3.350, the extra being Sensory). Thirteen cells are being compared against thirteen others across a 0.15 gap in what was measurable. That is the current posterior, not a hypothetical.

IT WENT LIVE TODAY, via ee258bf. Before it, optional held only Chart and Structural (both absent on this fixture) and Sensory was an always-present plain Double, so every blended cell carried the identical six terms. The defect was real in the code and INVISIBLE IN THE DATA. ee258bf is correct and stays; what it did was end the uniformity that was concealing this.

CHIEF'S PRECEDENT CORRECTED (third correction of my own ruling today). I said admitting a term to MayBeMissing is cost-neutral if its imputed value was zero. True of the SUM, worthless for the COMPARISON -- and in a COST, an imputed 0.0 means no penalty, which is indistinguishable from PERFECT AGREEMENT. So d_sens scored unmeasurable sensory agreement as perfect sensory agreement, harmlessly only while every cell got the same free pass. A uniform bias cancels in a comparison; a non-uniform one does not.

THE RULE THAT REPLACES IT: a term is safe in MayBeMissing only while its present-or-absent status is UNIFORM across the cells being compared. That is a property of the CORPUS, not the code -- it can flip with no edit to any line, so it cannot be enforced by review and must be asserted.

ASSIGNED to m1, which measured this and then explicitly offered rather than claimed. DESIGN PROPOSAL FIRST, no candidate, and m1 does not self-review -- the proposal goes to someone who did not take the measurement.

THE DESIGN QUESTION, deliberately open: when two cells have different present-term sets, what does comparing their costs mean? Normalising by present weight makes a 5-term and a 6-term cell equally confident, which is not obviously right. Carrying support beside the cost is a second answer. A third is that cells with unequal support are not comparable and the aligner must say so.
